model_annotation: Figure 3(a) displays the loss versus number of training steps (FLOPs) for several methods during training from scratch. The x-axis, labeled "FLOPs," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from approximately 1e11 to 1e14, with tick marks at regular intervals of 1e11, 1e12, 1e13, and 1e14. The y-axis, labeled "Loss w.r.t steps," is linear and ranges from 0 to approximately 3.5, with tick marks at intervals of 0.5. The plot contains five lines, each representing a different method: "Vanilla" (black solid line), "SrmLLM (n=380)" (red dashed line), "SepLLM (n=64)" (blue dash-dotted line), "SepLLM (n=256)" (green dotted line), and "SepLLM (n=64,H/T)" (purple solid line with markers). All lines start at a loss value of approximately 3.5 at 1e11 FLOPs and decrease as training progresses. The "Vanilla" method shows the steepest initial decline, reaching a loss of about 0.5 at 1e14 FLOPs. The "SrmLLM (n=380)" line starts slightly lower and declines more gradually, ending near 0.8. The "SepLLM (n=64)" and "SepLLM (n=256)" lines exhibit similar trends, with "SepLLM (n=256)" slightly outperforming "SepLLM (n=64)" by the end, both reaching losses around 0.6–0.7. The "SepLLM (n=64,H/T)" line follows a trajectory similar to "SepLLM (n=64)" but with a slightly lower final loss, approximately 0.6.
